title: Downscaling Satellite Soil Moisture Estimates with Machine Learning
author: Mario Guevara
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6cahase

steps.title: Prepare Prediction Factors
steps.instruction: Prepare the topographic prediction factors in R using the raster library, ensuring they are in a geographical coordinate system (+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs).

substeps.instruction: Load the 'raster' library.
Specify the path to the prediction factors (e.g., 'path/to/topographic/files') and list files with the '.sdat' pattern (or .tif, .asc, .img).
Create a raster stack of the files.
Define a function to replace NA values with the median of the layer.
Convert the raster stack to a 'SpatialPixelsDataFrame' object.
Apply the NA-to-median transformation to the data in the SpatialPixelsDataFrame.

steps.title: Prepare Response Variable
steps.instruction: Import and process the ESA-CCI satellite soil moisture data to match the prediction factors.

substeps.instruction: Download ESA-CCI soil moisture maps (*.nc files) and place them in the working directory.
Generate a list of annual soil moisture folders using list.dirs().
For a specific year (e.g., i=1 for 1991), stack the soil moisture records using the 'sm' variable name.
Crop the soil moisture raster to the extent of the prediction factors (x).
Calculate the median yearly value from the daily estimates using calc(r, median, na.rm=TRUE).

steps.title: Build Regression Matrix
steps.instruction: Create a data frame combining coordinates, soil moisture data, and terrain parameters.

substeps.instruction: Assign the projection (+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs) to the soil moisture raster (r).
Convert the raster to a data frame with coordinates (xy=T) and remove NA values.
Define the coordinate columns and assign the projection system to the data frame.
Overlay the soil moisture centroids with the prediction factors (x) using the over() function.
Combine the extracted values into a single data frame and remove NAs.
Create a training set 'z' containing the soil moisture value (column 3), coordinates (columns 1-2), and terrain parameters (columns 4-18).
Initialize an empty data frame 'results' with columns: year, cor, rmse, n, kernel, and k.

steps.title: Model Soil Moisture
steps.instruction: Develop a kernel-based machine learning model using 10-fold cross-validation to determine optimal parameters.

substeps.instruction: Load the 'kknn' library.
Perform 10-fold cross-validation using train.kknn() with kmax=50, distance=2, scale=TRUE, and test kernels: rectangular, triangular, epanechnikov, gaussian, rank, and optimal.
Identify the best kernel and optimal k from the tuning results.
Calculate the root mean squared error (RMSE) and the correlation (cd) between observed and predicted values.
Store the year, correlation, RMSE, number of observations (dim(z)[1]), best kernel, and best k in the 'results' data frame.

steps.title: Predict Across Area of Interest
steps.instruction: Apply the optimized model to the entire prediction domain to generate a digital soil moisture map.

substeps.instruction: Run the kknn() function using the training set 'z' and the prediction domain 'x' with the optimal kernel and k value.
Add the fitted prediction values to the 'x' SpatialPixelsDataFrame as a new column 'kknn'.
Convert the 'kknn' column into a raster object (r).
Save the resulting raster as a .tif file (e.g., 'predicted-1991-esa-sm-topo-CONUS.tif').
Save the accuracy report from the 'results' data frame as a .csv file (e.g., 'accuracy-1991-esa-sm-topo-CONUS.csv').
